name: Jasper Green
lede: Jasper Green is a muted, blue-leaning green named for jasper, the banded quartz usually associated with reds and browns rather than green.

sections.title: A less typical jasper
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 atlas gives this swatch at plate XXXIII, hue 37″, tone i, placed by the 1955 ISCC-NBS system in block 145, a moderate green [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary records a close variant, at plate 29, H 7, first used in 1905 [1]. Jasper is better known as a red or brown stone, so the green reading here is one of its less typical colors, closer to our library's Hooker's Green than to any red jasper [1].

The closest core app color is [[viridian]], under five units away, and Ridgway's plates also carry a near-duplicate he called Terre Verte, under two units off [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this green in 50 of 23,781 paintings, about a fifth of one per cent [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 9 of 1,674 paintings, at more than five times the overall baseline rate [2]. The earliest match is an undated 1490 Virgin and Child with Saint Anne, four centuries before Ridgway's plate, so that is a lookalike hue and not a pigment record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and a match is not evidence that jasper, or any mineral, was ground into the paint [2].
